cells.tense: Right now you are tending what is left with the same care you gave it while it was alive.
cells.ask: Name what this thing gave you, then finish the last task that belongs to it.
cells.core:
There is clearing happening and you are in the middle of it with your hands open. What stays, stays on purpose. What goes, goes because you decided it goes. You are not clinging and you are not cutting off; you are sorting with the same steadiness you brought when there was more to hold.

The ending is being met, not fought. Letting go here is the last form your care takes—not a failure of it, not a loss of grip. The old thing is not abandoned. It is finished, by someone who knew how to tend it. That is worth noticing while it is still happening, because the clearing is quiet and it would be easy to walk past your own part in it.
cells.sheetLine: You are letting go like someone who knows how to hold.

cells.tense: You are already living in the after, planning what goes in the cleared space before the space is clear.
cells.ask: Pick one thing that has ended and do the task that finishes it, not the task that starts what is next.
cells.core:
You are skipping the ending to get to the beginning. There is a version of this in your head where the transition is already done—the room rearranged, the next thing running—and you are pushing the present to match it. Clearing is not done because you decided it should be. It is done when the thing has actually been let go, and that is slower than the picture.

You are managing what has not arrived and leaving what is here half-finished. The door you keep stepping through in your mind has not opened yet. Come back to the one thing that is actually ending. It needs your hands for an hour, not your plans for a year.
cells.sheetLine: You are planning the next room before this one is cleared.

cells.tense: You are still standing in the doorway of a room you already left, not sure if you are allowed to be done.
cells.ask: Choose one object, habit, or commitment that has ended and set it down for a week.
cells.core:
The ending already happened and you have not caught up to it. Part of you is still checking on something that was let go—still carrying its weight, still giving it the attention that belongs to what is alive now. You are not refusing the clearing. You just have not fully arrived in it, and the load you keep lifting is no longer attached to anything.

Nothing is wrong with you for this. What you need is one plain thing to practice on. Pick a box, a task, a standing obligation that plainly belongs to what is over, and leave it alone for a stretch. Not forever. Seven days. Let your care show itself on something that is actually here.
cells.sheetLine: You are tending something that ended a while back.

cells.tense: You are clearing the room and calling it just being practical, as if the ending had nothing to do with you.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing you let go this month and why you chose to let it go.
cells.core:
You are already in the middle of the ending. Things are being sorted, decisions are being made, the space is changing—and you describe it as if it were simply happening, as if the shape of the room were decided by something other than your care. You are the one choosing what stays. You have been choosing it for a good stretch now.

This is not impersonal and it is not small. The judgment about what is finished and what is not has been yours. Letting go has been your work, not the work of circumstance. You can say so without making a ceremony of it. Let someone hear that you picked this, and that you picked it carefully.
cells.sheetLine: You chose what to release. You can say that out loud.
